note: Adjudications after the first score (which stays as measured), by an independent judge who did not author, read or settle these cases, under one convention: a good case becomes unknown when its RTL is correct only under a property of a top-level input that neither the RTL nor an SDC line that actually applies declares (raw-reset release timing into a register that can expose a mixed or metastable non-reset value, a reset assertion width the function relies on, or the launch clock of an input whose capture is unsafe if asynchronous); it stays good when the RTL is safe for any timing of those inputs. rfc1-b01 and b02 move from a frozen detection gap to expected rule RDC-009 once the rule covers exported resets. rfc1-b04, b05, b06 and b10 were reviewed under the same convention and stay good. cases.reason: 8-bit cfg releases from por_n, which has no input delay, while we can load wdata; a release in the recovery window can corrupt cfg and cfg_shadow; the twin rfc1-a02 is good only because por_n is constrained

reset release is safe by construction, but the valid_i input delay is not applied (-max/-min take no value), and an asynchronous valid_i directly enables the 8-bit count_q (convention 2: value from an unconstrained input)

the source-reset clear of the sticky status samples rst_a_n as a level in clk_b, so it relies on an undeclared minimum assertion width; RDC_WORKFLOW: an undeclared contract blocks any claim about reset pulse behaviour
